messages:
mike: Heads up — preparing the private installer v1.14.2 for the VPC customer cutover tonight. packaging is done but we hit a signer TTL warning in CI. anyone see the same?

sara: saw the CI alert. looks like the cosign signer rotated yesterday. manifest signer expired for the delta bundle.

mike: hmm. is that a hard blocker for the airgap handoff?

sara: depends. we can re-sign but that changes the manifest digest and would require a pin update on the customer's side. if they want no-change we need an authorized unpin window.

jen: @mike @sara short term option: create a signed-epoch tag and ship with a note to ops on how to fast-rollforward. longer term we should automate signer TTL renewal in the packaging job.

kevin: deploy-bot just reported the canary lane is free. recommend a staged canary (5 nodes) for 30m then promote. rollback criteria: any >3% checksum mismatch across mirrors OR cosign verify failures, or installer bootstrap failing on >1 instance.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] canary slot reserved: canary-3 (5 hosts). window=30m. artifacts pinned to tag=redwood-private-v1.14.2-signed-2026-03-21.

mike: link to release notes & manifest: https://internal.redwood/release/1.14.2/notes (private)

ops-oncall: quick question — do we need to rotate KMS access for the customer before shipping? they requested key rotation this cycle. if yes we should delay shipping until key handoff completes.

sara: they requested rotation but said it can be out-of-band. I recommend we ship signed artifacts now and coordination team will assist with key rotation post-delivery. we should add a bullet in the release notes about key rotation steps.

jen: agreed. documenting steps here so customer success can follow:
```
1. Download installer: s3://private-bucket/releases/redwood-v1.14.2-installer.tar.gz
2. Verify: cosign verify --key /path/to/customer.pub redwood-v1.14.2-installer.tar.gz
3. sha256sum redwood-v1.14.2-installer.tar.gz | grep <EXPECTED_SHA256>
```

kevin: testing results from staging: bootstrap success=100/100 hosts, agent-start latency median=220ms, KV cache priming passed. one mirror reported slow rsync in APAC (10-20s lag) — not a blocker but note in delivery runbook.

mike: decision call: do we proceed with canary now or hold for re-sign? proposal: proceed with current signed tag (re-signed by new signer) and mark previous manifest as deprecated. ops can patch customer pin via signed-epoch tag. all in favor?

ops-oncall: in favor, but add a rollback playbook to the thread and pin the rollback index. I can standby during the 30m window.

kevin: ACK. I'll push the signed tag and update deploy-bot. deploying canary in 5m.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] starting canary deploy -> tag=redwood-private-v1.14.2-signed-2026-03-21. canary hosts: canary-1, canary-2, canary-3, canary-4, canary-5. ETA 8m.

mike: copy that. ops-oncall, ping me if anything >1 failure.

(20 minutes later)

kevin: canary passed initial smoke (0 failures). mirror async lag still visible on mirror-3 but installer verified there too.

ops-oncall: saw one bootstrap timeout on canary-4 at 00:12:34 UTC, but retried and succeeded. marking it transient.

mike: good. promoting to full delivery in the next 10m. tag/pin to communicate: redwood-private-v1.14.2-signed-2026-03-21 -> pinned for customer rollout.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] promoting canary -> full rollout. expected duration 40m. fallback action: if >3% hosts fail within 10m, automatic rollback to tag=redwood-private-v1.14.1-stable will trigger.

jen: adding release note blurb for customer: "Installer v1.14.2 signed with new epoch key. If your deploy pin references a digest, update to tag redwood-private-v1.14.2-signed-2026-03-21 or follow the pinned-epoch instructions."

mike: Thanks team. filing a short post-release checklist: update customer pin, confirm KMS rotation handshake completed, archive old signer certs, close out the canary ticket.

kevin: noted. I'll open a follow-on ticket for automating signer TTL renewals in packager.

mike: thread resolved for now. :tada:
